raw_graphql_pull_request.body: > Closed at the author's request to split this work. The three standalone PRs are #8495 (quantized-rollout sentinel), #8513 (post-sync MXFP8 self-check and SGLang sync guards), and #8514 (quantized-layer audit). Each targets official main directly; the original fork branches and validation history are retained. > Scope distinction: #8486 checks startup weight-transfer repeatability by hashing two loads. #8513 compares sampled kernel outputs against canonical references after every sync; #8514 checks training/export/receiver agreement about which layers are quantized. They cover different failure modes. The fork's BF16 MoE fix already present on main is not duplicated in #8513. ### What does this PR do? The rest of #7519 after #8127: refit fixes and runtime checks for quantized (MXFP8) rollouts, on top of #8287, #8306 and #8308. - **vLLM refit**: MoE layers kept in BF16 by `rollout.quantization.ignore` are re-derived after every quantized refit. Before, the quantized refit left them in their load-time kernel layout: with vLLM's FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE kernel the first sync failed with a shape error, and with FlashInfer CUTLASS gate and up would have been swapped silently. - **SGLang refit** (on #8306): two configurations are refused before anything is written: BF16 MoE layers whose runner re-laid out the experts at load (SGLang's FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner does; verl's default DeepGEMM runner keeps them in checkpoint layout), and the delta checkpoint engine with any quantized rollout (#8306 refused it only for the formats on its refit loader). - **Three checks**, each `warn` by default (log and keep going), `raise` or `0` through an environment variable: - post-sync self-check: after every sync, one dense MXFP8 layer and one expert run through their own kernels against a dequantized reference (vLLM and SGLang); - quantized-layer audit, two comparisons, each once: training vs export, when training runs a TE FP8 recipe, at the first weight sync after a training step; export vs engine, for any quantized rollout, inside each engine's weight loader on the first weight sync, before each bucket is written (one implementation for vLLM and SGLang); - quantized-rollout sentinel: NaN log-probs, runaway KL, every response at the length cap. - **Docs**: a Checks section in `docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md`, and the format check in `docs/low_precision/qat.md`. This is #8314 without the training recipe, which #8127 merged, rebased onto main and adapted to #8308 (DeepGEMM is now a default that `engine_kwargs` override, and `VERL_ROLLOUT_USE_DEEP_GEMM` is gone). It replaces #8128, #8130, #8131 and #8132 from #7519's split. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs: [mxfp8](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+mxfp8), [quantized refit](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+refit+quantized). Besides #7519's own split, which this replaces, #7186 quantizes rollout weights to MXFP8 on the SGLang side (rollout only, before #8306), and #8293 keeps vLLM's auto-selected DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 MoE backend refittable. Neither adds these checks or fixes. - [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`. ### Test CPU tests, with compressed-tensors 0.17.0; vLLM, SGLang and TE are stubbed where needed: ```bash python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_sglang_quant_refit_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_unquant_utils_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_quant_layer_audit_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_quant_sentinel_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_quant_sync_format_check_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_weight_update_utils_on_cpu.py # 168 passed ``` The other CPU tests that import the modules this PR changes give the same results as on main (67bf1df3) in this environment, failures included; `tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py`, which fails here for want of a full vLLM install, passes with ba2852ec under vLLM 0.29.0 on the B200 machine. `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files. ### B200 validation **This branch on 1×B200 (3ab3b20b, then ba2852ec)**: a tiny random Qwen3-MoE (2 layers, 8 experts, top-2) on GSM8K and an MXFP8 rollout on each engine's defaults since #8308; vLLM 0.29.0, SGLang 0.5.20, Transformer Engine 2.16.1, Megatron-Core 0.19.2. 2 GRPO steps per run, with the self-check, the audit and the sentinel in `raise` mode (the sentinel's length-cap rule off: this random model's responses hit the cap from step 1). In the fault runs, a test hook sends layer 0's `o_proj` in BF16 instead of FP8 after the training-vs-export audit has recorded it, so only the engine side sees the wrong format. | run | training | result | |---|---|---| | vLLM and SGLang, defaults | MXFP8 (TE `fp8_recipe=mxfp8`) | passes on both: the format check finished at the first sync (69 weights checked, none in another format, none unmapped), training vs export agreed after step 1, and the self-check passed after every sync (dense 0.026; experts 0.048 on vLLM, 0.047 on SGLang); `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0020–0.0025 (vLLM) and 0.0006–0.0008 (SGLang) | | vLLM and SGLang, defaults | BF16 | passes on both: training vs export is not armed, the format check still runs (69 / 0 / 0), and the self-check passes (dense 0.026, experts 0.046–0.049); `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0021–0.0040 and 0.0004–0.0014 | | SGLang, `o_proj` sent in BF16 | MXFP8 and BF16 | the format check reports that weight and no other (`the sync sends bfloat16, the engine parameter is float8_e4m3fn`) and stops before its bucket is written; the error ends SGLang's scheduler, which takes the server down, and the run fails 11–12 s later, before step 1 | | vLLM, `o_proj` sent in BF16, on 3ab3b20b | MXFP8 and BF16 | the same report, also before the write, but the run then hung until stopped (281 s and 169 s later): the error is raised inside the receiver's bucket callback, so that bucket is never acked, and the trainer's `BucketedWeightSender` waits for each ack with no timeout, so `update_weights` never reaches the `await` that carries the error | | vLLM, `o_proj` sent in BF16, on ba2852ec | MXFP8 | the run fails 5 s after the report, before step 1; the trainer's traceback ends with the format check's message | | vLLM, defaults, on ba2852ec | MXFP8 | passes, as on 3ab3b20b: 69 / 0 / 0, training vs export agreed, dense 0.026, experts 0.048, `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0021 | ba2852ec keeps the first error raised while a bucket loads, acks the remaining buckets without loading them, and raises once the sender is done, as the delta path already does. The same hang follows any error raised while a bucket loads, on main too. Rollout TP 2 needs two GPUs and was not run. On SGLang 0.5.20, Qwen3-MoE builds its experts without `reduce_results` and all-reduces after them, so at rollout TP > 1 the expert probe skips with one warning per worker, as `mxfp8.md` documents; the dense probe still runs. **Earlier on this branch (cf32f6ae)**, same model and versions, 5 GRPO steps per run, the self-check and the audit in `raise` mode unless noted. These cover the self-check's failure path and the refit fixes and refusals; the refit and refusal code (`vllm_unquant_utils.py`, `vllm_quant_utils.py`, `sglang_fp8_utils.py`) and the self-check's comparison (`mxfp8_refit_check.py`) have not changed since. | run | rollout kernels | result | |---|---|---| | vLLM, defaults | experts on DeepGEMM; dense on FlashInfer CuTe-DSL (vLLM 0.29 has no DeepGEMM MXFP8 dense kernel) | passes: the self-check passed after every sync (dense 0.026, experts 0.048), the audit agreed, `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0021–0.0026 | | SGLang, defaults | DeepGEMM | passes: self-check dense 0.026, experts 0.047; `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0003–0.0008 | | vLLM and SGLang, every MXFP8 expert scale corrupted after each sync (test hook) | as above | the MoE self-check stops the run at the first sync (SGLang: 3.36 against 0.047) | | vLLM and SGLang, entropy bonus 0.01 so the synced weights change every step | as above | passes: non-zero gradients; the self-check error changes from sync to sync (experts 0.0467–0.0488 and 0.0469–0.0481) and stays within tolerance | | vLLM, layer 1's experts in BF16, `moe_backend=flashinfer_trtllm` | TRT-LLM for the MXFP8 and the BF16 experts | passes: all six syncs go through with the BF16 layer; before this PR's fix, the first sync failed in `_load_w13` | | SGLang, every expert in BF16 (`re:.*mlp\.experts\..*`) | DeepGEMM | passes: the BF16 MoE refusal does not fire, and the syncs go through | Without the entropy bonus, the random model's reward is always 0, so its weights do not change between syncs; the entropy-bonus runs cover changing weights. **Earlier runs**, on #8314's code before its rebase onto #8306 and #8308: - **Qwen3-30B-A3B on 4×B200**, MXFP8 training and MXFP8 vLLM rollout (training TP2 / EP2, rollout TP2, DAPO-Math-17k, 5 GRPO steps, audit in `raise` mode): - all 5 steps ran, with `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0037–0.0040; - 24 dense and 24 expert self-checks passed (0.0016–0.0017 and 0.045–0.046); - the audit agreed on 48 of 48 decoder layers (18,817 weights), and the engine re-check matched all 18,867 synced weights; - FlashInfer was not available to vLLM's workers in that image, so vLLM ran Marlin dense GEMMs (BF16 activations, hence the low dense error) and DeepGEMM experts, the expert kernel #8308 now requests by default. - **A tiny Qwen3-MoE on 1×B200**, vLLM with FlashInfer TRT-LLM forced for the dense layers and the experts, every check in `raise` mode: the self-check passed after every sync (dense 0.026, experts 0.052), the audit agreed on 2 of 2 decoder layers (69 weights), and `rollout_corr/kl` read 0.0019–0.0024. The sentinel's length-cap rule raised at step 5: this randomly initialized model's responses all hit the cap from step 1, which the rule cannot tell from a broken rollout. - **BF16 MoE layers under a quantized vLLM refit** (1×B200, vLLM 0.29, a small Qwen3-MoE with layer 1's experts in `ignore`, expert 0 of that layer compared with a BF16 reference after every sync): - before the fix, on vLLM's FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend: the first sync failed in `_load_w13` (`shard_dim=0 is not a valid data dimension for a 3D tensor`); - after it: the layer was re-derived from `[8, 512, 512]` into `[8, 8, 512, 64]`, and the expert matched at 0.0022–0.0024 on all 5 syncs (0.50 against a gate/up-swapped reference); - on the Triton backend, which vLLM picks without FlashInfer, both versions passed. - **SGLang**: the BF16 MoE refusal covers a failure measured on 1×B200 with SGLang 0.5.20 on its TRT-LLM MoE runner (`FusedMoE._load_w13` at the first sync). ### Found on main while validating (not from this PR) - **vLLM refuses MoE layers kept in BF16 since #8308.** verl requests `moe_backend=deep_gemm` for quantized rollouts, and vLLM 0.29 rejects it for unquantized MoE layers instead of falling back: `ValueError: moe_backend='deep_gemm' is not supported for unquantized MoE. Expected one of ['triton', 'batched_triton', 'flashinfer_trtllm', 'flashinfer_cutlass', 'aiter']`. Any quantized vLLM rollout whose `rollout.quantization.ignore` covers experts now fails at engine start. Setting `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.moe_backend` explicitly (for example `flashinfer_trtllm`, as in the run above) avoids it; a fix would leave `moe_backend` unset when some MoE layers stay in BF16. - **The exporter and SGLang read `ignore` differently (#8306).** `_translate_ignored_layers` passes plain names to SGLang, which matches them as prefixes, while the trainer-side exporter matches exact module names or `re:` patterns. With `ignore: ["model.layers.0"]`, SGLang keeps layer 0 in BF16 but the exporter still quantizes it. This PR's export-vs-engine check (`VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT`) refuses that sync in `raise` mode (28 weights, measured on cf32f6ae); in the default `warn` mode it logs the disagreement and the FP8 bytes are loaded into the BF16 parameters. For MoE layers, `re:.*mlp\.experts\..*` (all experts) is the only pattern both read the same way today. Neither is changed in this PR. ### API and Usage Example No config or API change. New environment switches, each `warn` (default), `raise` or `0`: - `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK`: the post-sync self-check, with `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL` / `_MOE_TOL`; - `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT`: both comparisons of the audit, with `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT_TRACE` for the training side; - `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL`: the sentinel, with `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX` / `_CLIP_STEPS`. ```bash # stop the sync instead of logging when a kernel layout did not follow it export VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=raise ``` ### Design & Code Changes - vLLM: `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_unquant_utils.py`, `vllm_quant_utils.py` (BF16 MoE re-derivation; self-check hooks); `vllm_mxfp8_refit_check.py` (new); `vllm_sync_format_check.py` (new: the parameter each synced weight lands in); `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py` (the format check around the quantized load; an error raised while a bucket loads now surfaces after the transfer handshake instead of leaving the trainer waiting). - SGLang, on #8306: `verl/utils/sglang/sglang_fp8_utils.py` (BF16 MoE refusal; `0xFF` staging and the unwritten-scale check); `sglang_quant_utils.py` (delta refusal; format check and self-check in the refit loader); `sglang_mxfp8_refit_check.py` (new); `sglang_sync_format_check.py` (new); `verl/workers/rollout/sglang_rollout/sglang_rollout.py` (delta refusal at adapter init and at sync). - Checks, all new: `verl/utils/mxfp8_refit_check.py` (self-check), `quant_layer_audit.py` (training vs export), `quant_sync_format_check.py` (export vs engine, shared by both engines), `quant_sentinel.py`; hooks in `verl/workers/engine_workers.py`, `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`, `verl/utils/megatron_utils.py`, `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`, `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`. - Docs: a Checks section in `docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md`; the format check in `docs/low_precision/qat.md`. ### AI assistance disclosure Developed with AI assistance. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and the B200 experiments above, and can defend the change end to end. ### Checklist Before Submitting - [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting). - [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): `docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md`, `docs/low_precision/qat.md`. - [x] Add unit test(s): the CPU tests above (`*_on_cpu.py`, run by CI); hardware evidence above. - [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the [`ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1).

Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The inspected mutation and abort paths affect loaded model weights, rollout availability, and trainer ranks participating in the same synchronization job. The evidence does not establish a cross-tenant attack path or additional credential, host, or infrastructure authority. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The inspected checks consume trainer-exported tensors, model quantization configuration, engine module state, and training metrics. Environment configuration controls diagnostic enforcement. These checks validate numerical and format consistency; they do not authenticate weight provenance or authorize callers. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — The layer audit records its training verdict or engine-query attempt before raising a mismatch. Those audit states are one-shot rather than persistent failure latches. The inspected normal training calls do not demonstrate an automatic recovery path, so safe in-process retry after a strict failure remains unestablished. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — If recovery without restarting the job is intended, define a coordinated all-rank abort and retry contract: prevent serving until validation succeeds, restore owned resources, and preserve failed audit verdicts until explicitly corrected or revalidated.

**Use the configured generation cap for the V1 clip check.**

If every response ends at the same short length, `data.to_padded_tensor()` makes that length the response tensor’s width. `compute_data_metrics` then reports `response_length/clip_ratio == 1` even though no response reached the generation cap. Compare response lengths with the configured cap or use explicit truncation data before applying the streak rule.

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Mark the engine recheck as asked when the query fails.**

If `quant_methods_of` raises, the code logs a warning and returns. `auditor._rechecked` stays `False`, so `wants_engine_recheck()` stays `True`.

Every later `update_weights` call then repeats the failing RPC and the warning. This happens, for example, when a custom vLLM worker class lacks `quant_layer_audit_methods`. The `QuantLayerAuditor` docstring says a rank that cannot be asked counts as asked.

Call `auditor.recheck_against_engine(None)` in the `except` block. This applies the same one-shot rule that the `None` result path already uses.

detail.body: > Closed at the author's request to split this work. The three standalone PRs are #8495 (quantized-rollout sentinel), #8513 (post-sync MXFP8 self-check and SGLang sync guards), and #8514 (quantized-layer audit). Each targets official main directly; the original fork branches and validation history are retained. > Scope distinction: #8486 checks startup weight-transfer repeatability by hashing two loads. #8513 compares sampled kernel outputs against canonical references after every sync; #8514 checks training/export/receiver agreement about which layers are quantized. They cover different failure modes. The fork's BF16 MoE fix already present on main is not duplicated in #8513. ### What does this PR do? The rest of #7519 after #8127: refit fixes and runtime checks for quantized (MXFP8) rollouts, on top of #8287, #8306 and #8308. - **vLLM refit**: MoE layers kept in BF16 by `rollout.quantization.ignore` are re-derived after every quantized refit. Before, the quantized refit left them in their load-time kernel layout: with vLLM's FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE kernel the first sync failed with a shape error, and with FlashInfer CUTLASS gate and up would have been swapped silently. - **SGLang refit** (on #8306): two configurations are refused before anything is written: BF16 MoE layers whose runner re-laid out the experts at load (SGLang's FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner does; verl's default DeepGEMM runner keeps them in checkpoint layout), and the delta checkpoint engine with any quantized rollout (#8306 refused it only for the formats on its refit loader). - **Three checks**, each `warn` by default (log and keep going), `raise` or `0` through an environment variable: - post-sync self-check: after every sync, one dense MXFP8 layer and one expert run through their own kernels against a dequantized reference (vLLM and SGLang); - quantized-layer audit, two comparisons, each once: training vs export, when training runs a TE FP8 recipe, at the first weight sync after a training step; export vs engine, for any quantized rollout, inside each engine's weight loader on the first weight sync, before each bucket is written (one implementation for vLLM and SGLang); - quantized-rollout sentinel: NaN log-probs, runaway KL, every response at the length cap. - **Docs**: a Checks section in `docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md`, and the format check in `docs/low_precision/qat.md`. This is #8314 without the training recipe, which #8127 merged, rebased onto main and adapted to #8308 (DeepGEMM is now a default that `engine_kwargs` override, and `VERL_ROLLOUT_USE_DEEP_GEMM` is gone). It replaces #8128, #8130, #8131 and #8132 from #7519's split. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs: [mxfp8](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+mxfp8), [quantized refit](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+refit+quantized). Besides #7519's own split, which this replaces, #7186 quantizes rollout weights to MXFP8 on the SGLang side (rollout only, before #8306), and #8293 keeps vLLM's auto-selected DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 MoE backend refittable. Neither adds these checks or fixes. - [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`. ### Test CPU tests, with compressed-tensors 0.17.0; vLLM, SGLang and TE are stubbed where needed: ```bash python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_sglang_quant_refit_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_unquant_utils_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_quant_layer_audit_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_quant_sentinel_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_quant_sync_format_check_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_weight_update_utils_on_cpu.py # 168 passed ``` The other CPU tests that import the modules this PR changes give the same results as on main (67bf1df3) in this environment, failures included; `tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py`, which fails here for want of a full vLLM install, passes with ba2852ec under vLLM 0.29.0 on the B200 machine. `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files. ### B200 validation **This branch on 1×B200 (3ab3b20b, then ba2852ec)**: a tiny random Qwen3-MoE (2 layers, 8 experts, top-2) on GSM8K and an MXFP8 rollout on each engine's defaults since #8308; vLLM 0.29.0, SGLang 0.5.20, Transformer Engine 2.16.1, Megatron-Core 0.19.2. 2 GRPO steps per run, with the self-check, the audit and the sentinel in `raise` mode (the sentinel's length-cap rule off: this random model's responses hit the cap from step 1). In the fault runs, a test hook sends layer 0's `o_proj` in BF16 instead of FP8 after the training-vs-export audit has recorded it, so only the engine side sees the wrong format. | run | training | result | |---|---|---| | vLLM and SGLang, defaults | MXFP8 (TE `fp8_recipe=mxfp8`) | passes on both: the format check finished at the first sync (69 weights checked, none in another format, none unmapped), training vs export agreed after step 1, and the self-check passed after every sync (dense 0.026; experts 0.048 on vLLM, 0.047 on SGLang); `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0020–0.0025 (vLLM) and 0.0006–0.0008 (SGLang) | | vLLM and SGLang, defaults | BF16 | passes on both: training vs export is not armed, the format check still runs (69 / 0 / 0), and the self-check passes (dense 0.026, experts 0.046–0.049); `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0021–0.0040 and 0.0004–0.0014 | | SGLang, `o_proj` sent in BF16 | MXFP8 and BF16 | the format check reports that weight and no other (`the sync sends bfloat16, the engine parameter is float8_e4m3fn`) and stops before its bucket is written; the error ends SGLang's scheduler, which takes the server down, and the run fails 11–12 s later, before step 1 | | vLLM, `o_proj` sent in BF16, on 3ab3b20b | MXFP8 and BF16 | the same report, also before the write, but the run then hung until stopped (281 s and 169 s later): the error is raised inside the receiver's bucket callback, so that bucket is never acked, and the trainer's `BucketedWeightSender` waits for each ack with no timeout, so `update_weights` never reaches the `await` that carries the error | | vLLM, `o_proj` sent in BF16, on ba2852ec | MXFP8 | the run fails 5 s after the report, before step 1; the trainer's traceback ends with the format check's message | | vLLM, defaults, on ba2852ec | MXFP8 | passes, as on 3ab3b20b: 69 / 0 / 0, training vs export agreed, dense 0.026, experts 0.048, `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0021 | ba2852ec keeps the first error raised while a bucket loads, acks the remaining buckets without loading them, and raises once the sender is done, as the delta path already does. The same hang follows any error raised while a bucket loads, on main too. Rollout TP 2 needs two GPUs and was not run. On SGLang 0.5.20, Qwen3-MoE builds its experts without `reduce_results` and all-reduces after them, so at rollout TP > 1 the expert probe skips with one warning per worker, as `mxfp8.md` documents; the dense probe still runs. **Earlier on this branch (cf32f6ae)**, same model and versions, 5 GRPO steps per run, the self-check and the audit in `raise` mode unless noted. These cover the self-check's failure path and the refit fixes and refusals; the refit and refusal code (`vllm_unquant_utils.py`, `vllm_quant_utils.py`, `sglang_fp8_utils.py`) and the self-check's comparison (`mxfp8_refit_check.py`) have not changed since. | run | rollout kernels | result | |---|---|---| | vLLM, defaults | experts on DeepGEMM; dense on FlashInfer CuTe-DSL (vLLM 0.29 has no DeepGEMM MXFP8 dense kernel) | passes: the self-check passed after every sync (dense 0.026, experts 0.048), the audit agreed, `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0021–0.0026 | | SGLang, defaults | DeepGEMM | passes: self-check dense 0.026, experts 0.047; `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0003–0.0008 | | vLLM and SGLang, every MXFP8 expert scale corrupted after each sync (test hook) | as above | the MoE self-check stops the run at the first sync (SGLang: 3.36 against 0.047) | | vLLM and SGLang, entropy bonus 0.01 so the synced weights change every step | as above | passes: non-zero gradients; the self-check error changes from sync to sync (experts 0.0467–0.0488 and 0.0469–0.0481) and stays within tolerance | | vLLM, layer 1's experts in BF16, `moe_backend=flashinfer_trtllm` | TRT-LLM for the MXFP8 and the BF16 experts | passes: all six syncs go through with the BF16 layer; before this PR's fix, the first sync failed in `_load_w13` | | SGLang, every expert in BF16 (`re:.*mlp\.experts\..*`) | DeepGEMM | passes: the BF16 MoE refusal does not fire, and the syncs go through | Without the entropy bonus, the random model's reward is always 0, so its weights do not change between syncs; the entropy-bonus runs cover changing weights. **Earlier runs**, on #8314's code before its rebase onto #8306 and #8308: - **Qwen3-30B-A3B on 4×B200**, MXFP8 training and MXFP8 vLLM rollout (training TP2 / EP2, rollout TP2, DAPO-Math-17k, 5 GRPO steps, audit in `raise` mode): - all 5 steps ran, with `rollout_corr/kl` 0.0037–0.0040; - 24 dense and 24 expert self-checks passed (0.0016–0.0017 and 0.045–0.046); - the audit agreed on 48 of 48 decoder layers (18,817 weights), and the engine re-check matched all 18,867 synced weights; - FlashInfer was not available to vLLM's workers in that image, so vLLM ran Marlin dense GEMMs (BF16 activations, hence the low dense error) and DeepGEMM experts, the expert kernel #8308 now requests by default. - **A tiny Qwen3-MoE on 1×B200**, vLLM with FlashInfer TRT-LLM forced for the dense layers and the experts, every check in `raise` mode: the self-check passed after every sync (dense 0.026, experts 0.052), the audit agreed on 2 of 2 decoder layers (69 weights), and `rollout_corr/kl` read 0.0019–0.0024. The sentinel's length-cap rule raised at step 5: this randomly initialized model's responses all hit the cap from step 1, which the rule cannot tell from a broken rollout. - **BF16 MoE layers under a quantized vLLM refit** (1×B200, vLLM 0.29, a small Qwen3-MoE with layer 1's experts in `ignore`, expert 0 of that layer compared with a BF16 reference after every sync): - before the fix, on vLLM's FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend: the first sync failed in `_load_w13` (`shard_dim=0 is not a valid data dimension for a 3D tensor`); - after it: the layer was re-derived from `[8, 512, 512]` into `[8, 8, 512, 64]`, and the expert matched at 0.0022–0.0024 on all 5 syncs (0.50 against a gate/up-swapped reference); - on the Triton backend, which vLLM picks without FlashInfer, both versions passed. - **SGLang**: the BF16 MoE refusal covers a failure measured on 1×B200 with SGLang 0.5.20 on its TRT-LLM MoE runner (`FusedMoE._load_w13` at the first sync). ### Found on main while validating (not from this PR) - **vLLM refuses MoE layers kept in BF16 since #8308.** verl requests `moe_backend=deep_gemm` for quantized rollouts, and vLLM 0.29 rejects it for unquantized MoE layers instead of falling back: `ValueError: moe_backend='deep_gemm' is not supported for unquantized MoE. Expected one of ['triton', 'batched_triton', 'flashinfer_trtllm', 'flashinfer_cutlass', 'aiter']`. Any quantized vLLM rollout whose `rollout.quantization.ignore` covers experts now fails at engine start. Setting `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.moe_backend` explicitly (for example `flashinfer_trtllm`, as in the run above) avoids it; a fix would leave `moe_backend` unset when some MoE layers stay in BF16. - **The exporter and SGLang read `ignore` differently (#8306).** `_translate_ignored_layers` passes plain names to SGLang, which matches them as prefixes, while the trainer-side exporter matches exact module names or `re:` patterns. With `ignore: ["model.layers.0"]`, SGLang keeps layer 0 in BF16 but the exporter still quantizes it. This PR's export-vs-engine check (`VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT`) refuses that sync in `raise` mode (28 weights, measured on cf32f6ae); in the default `warn` mode it logs the disagreement and the FP8 bytes are loaded into the BF16 parameters. For MoE layers, `re:.*mlp\.experts\..*` (all experts) is the only pattern both read the same way today. Neither is changed in this PR. ### API and Usage Example No config or API change. New environment switches, each `warn` (default), `raise` or `0`: - `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK`: the post-sync self-check, with `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL` / `_MOE_TOL`; - `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT`: both comparisons of the audit, with `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT_TRACE` for the training side; - `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL`: the sentinel, with `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX` / `_CLIP_STEPS`. ```bash # stop the sync instead of logging when a kernel layout did not follow it export VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=raise ``` ### Design & Code Changes - vLLM: `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_unquant_utils.py`, `vllm_quant_utils.py` (BF16 MoE re-derivation; self-check hooks); `vllm_mxfp8_refit_check.py` (new); `vllm_sync_format_check.py` (new: the parameter each synced weight lands in); `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py` (the format check around the quantized load; an error raised while a bucket loads now surfaces after the transfer handshake instead of leaving the trainer waiting). - SGLang, on #8306: `verl/utils/sglang/sglang_fp8_utils.py` (BF16 MoE refusal; `0xFF` staging and the unwritten-scale check); `sglang_quant_utils.py` (delta refusal; format check and self-check in the refit loader); `sglang_mxfp8_refit_check.py` (new); `sglang_sync_format_check.py` (new); `verl/workers/rollout/sglang_rollout/sglang_rollout.py` (delta refusal at adapter init and at sync). - Checks, all new: `verl/utils/mxfp8_refit_check.py` (self-check), `quant_layer_audit.py` (training vs export), `quant_sync_format_check.py` (export vs engine, shared by both engines), `quant_sentinel.py`; hooks in `verl/workers/engine_workers.py`, `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`, `verl/utils/megatron_utils.py`, `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`, `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`. - Docs: a Checks section in `docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md`; the format check in `docs/low_precision/qat.md`. ### AI assistance disclosure Developed with AI assistance. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and the B200 experiments above, and can defend the change end to end. ### Checklist Before Submitting - [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting). - [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): `docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md`, `docs/low_precision/qat.md`. - [x] Add unit test(s): the CPU tests above (`*_on_cpu.py`, run by CI); hardware evidence above. - [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the [`ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1).

@@ -50,6 +50,97 @@ Notes:
 verl defaults the MXFP8 dense and MoE kernels of vLLM and SGLang to DeepGEMM; for details, see
 [Low-Precision Rollout and Quantization-Aware Training](qat.md).
 
+## Checks
+
+![The quantized-rollout sentinel, the post-sync self-check and the quantized-layer audit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/031f882a-9379-4ef7-bbce-3a746959d317)
+
+| Check | Runs | Reports | Switch |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Quantized-rollout sentinel | every training step | NaN log-probs, KL above 1.0, every response at the length cap | `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL` |
+| Post-sync self-check | after every weight sync | kernel scale layouts that did not follow the sync | `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK` |
+| Quantized-layer audit | training vs export: first weight sync after a training step; export vs engine: first weight sync, before each bucket is written | layers that training, the exported weights and the engine quantize differently | `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT` |
+
+Each switch takes `warn` (the default: log the finding and keep going), `raise` (stop the run or the sync)
+or `0` (off). The sentinel applies to every quantized rollout, FP8 and FP4 included, and so does the audit's
+export-vs-engine comparison (on SGLang, to the formats of its refit loader: MXFP8, MXFP4, NVFP4).
+
+### Quantized-rollout sentinel
+
+When the rollout is quantized, both trainers check each step's metrics:
+
+- `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` is non-finite while the batch had valid tokens;
+- `rollout_corr/kl` is non-finite or above `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX` (default 1.0; healthy quantized
+  rollouts read about 0.001–0.03);
+- every response hits the length cap (`response_length/clip_ratio` close to 1) on
+  `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_CLIP_STEPS` consecutive steps (default 2; `0` turns this rule off, and it is off
+  under `rollout.ignore_eos`, where every response runs to the cap by design).
+
+The rollout counts as quantized when `rollout.quantization` sets `linear`, `moe` or `config_file`, or the
+model's own `config.json` (local paths only) carries a `quantization_config`. The sentinel catches gross
+failures only: one layer type left unquantized (KL 0.007–0.010) stays within the healthy range.
+
+### Post-sync self-check
+
+After loading, both engines derive kernel-specific copies of the MXFP8 weights and scales (swizzled
+scales, shuffled or packed experts). If a sync skips that step, the kernel pairs fresh weights with stale
+scales while every shape and dtype still matches. After every sync, verl therefore runs the smallest MXFP8
+linear layer and one expert of the smallest MXFP8 MoE layer through their own kernels on a small random
+input and compares the output with a BF16 reference on the dequantized canonical weights. Healthy layers
+read a relative error of about 0.03 (dense) and 0.05 (experts); a stale layout reads O(1).
+
+- `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL` (default 0.25) and `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL` set the thresholds.
+- On SGLang, the refit loader also reports experts whose scales the sync did not write.
+- The expert probe is skipped, with a warning, where its made-up routing cannot send every row to one
+  expert at weight 1. On vLLM: expert or data parallelism, non-SiLU gates, and, on monolithic MoE kernels, a
+  routed scaling factor, grouped top-k, a score correction bias or custom routing. On SGLang: expert
+  parallelism, TP without `reduce_results`, and non-softmax, grouped, biased or custom routing.
+
+What it does not show:
+
+- It samples one dense layer and one expert per sync; a layer outside the sample can still be stale.
+- It runs the kernels eagerly. A re-derivation into new storage, instead of the storage a CUDA graph
+  captured, passes the probe while graph replays keep reading the old values. That the captured storage is
+  updated rests on indirect evidence (the re-derived layouts are copied back in place, and the KL stays in
+  its healthy range), not on a graph replay.
+
+### Quantized-layer audit
+
+Three parties decide which layers are quantized, each on its own: training implicitly (TE linear modules
+inside `fp8_autocast`), and by name the trainer-side exporter and the engine, both from the same quantization
+config (`rollout.quantization`, or the checkpoint's own `quantization_config`). The audit compares them in two
+steps, each once:
+
+- **Training vs export**, when training runs a TE FP8 recipe, at the first weight sync after a training step
+  (the sync before it has no FP8 trace yet): each decoder layer's FP8 trace (TE's FP8 weight workspaces)
+  against the format the sync sends for that layer's GEMM projections (attention, MLP, experts,
+  linear-attention and SSM in / out projections). Weights the exporter keeps in BF16 by design are skipped.
+  Other decoder-layer weights, such as a convolution, are not judged, and the audit reports how many it left
+  out.
+- **Export vs engine**, whenever the rollout is quantized, during the first weight sync: inside the engine's
+  weight loader, before each bucket is written, every incoming weight's format (quantized or high
+  precision) against the engine parameter that receives it. vLLM checks every quantized format; SGLang
+  checks the formats of its refit loader (MXFP8, MXFP4, NVFP4). Later syncs send the same formats and are
+  not checked again.
+
+`VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT` switches both. `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT_TRACE=1` logs each step of the training-side
+comparison. The training-side trace is per layer,
+so a TE module kept in BF16 inside an FP8 layer would go unnoticed (Megatron has no such per-module option
+today). With `disable_parameter_transpose_cache=True` TE keeps no FP8 workspace, and the audit warns once
+that it cannot run.
+
+### Configurations SGLang refuses
+
+Two configurations are refused before a weight sync writes anything:
+
+- MoE layers kept in BF16 (`rollout.quantization.ignore`) whose experts the MoE runner re-laid out at load:
+  SGLang's FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner stores BF16 experts in a block layout a weight sync cannot write, while
+  verl's default DeepGEMM runner keeps them in checkpoint layout.
+- The delta checkpoint engine with any quantized rollout (`rollout.quantization` or the checkpoint's own
+  `quantization_config`): it applies its payloads without the trainer-side weight quantization.
+
+Do not set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` for an SGLang rollout: verl starts SGLang
+with `enable_memory_saver=True`, which refuses that allocator mode.
+
 ## Example: Qwen3-8B on GSM8K
 
 [`examples/mxfp8/run_qwen3_8b_megatron.sh`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/examples/mxfp8/run_qwen3_8b_megatron.sh)

@@ -247,6 +247,17 @@ SGLang uses the default CUDA Graph configuration):
 | Blackwell | SGLang | ❌ | NVFP4 MoE | FlashInfer CUTLASS (MoE; BF16 Linear) | 0.00946 |
 | Blackwell | SGLang | ❌ | NVFP4 MoE + NVFP4 QAT | FlashInfer CUTLASS (MoE; BF16 Linear) | 0.00653 |
 
+## Format check at the first weight sync
+
+When the rollout is quantized (QAT included), the engine compares, during the first weight sync and before each
+bucket is written, every synced weight's format (quantized or high precision) with the engine parameter that
+receives it. The trainer-side exporter and the engine read the same quantization config, so a disagreement means
+the two matched a module differently, for example an `ignore` entry one side reads as a prefix and the other as an
+exact name; loading would cast the weight into a parameter of the other format. vLLM checks every quantized
+format; SGLang checks the formats of its refit loader (MXFP8, MXFP4, NVFP4), not `FP8_BLOCK`.
+`VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT` switches it: `warn` (the default) logs the disagreement, `raise` stops the sync, `0`
+turns it off. See also the [checks of the MXFP8 recipe](mxfp8.md#checks).
+

 - SGLang MXFP8, MXFP4 and NVFP4 custom refit requires the default bucketed

+"""CPU tests for the MXFP8 post-refit self-check (dequant reference + probe)."""
+
+import logging
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.mxfp8_refit_check import (
+    assert_mxfp8_linear_matches,
+    assert_mxfp8_moe_expert_matches,
+    mxfp8_dequantize,
+    mxfp8_moe_expert_reference,
+    probe_mxfp8_linear,
+    probe_mxfp8_moe_expert,
+)
+
+N, K = 16, 128
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _check_raises(monkeypatch):
+    # These tests exercise the failure path; the default mode (warn) has its own tests below.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK", "raise")
+
+
+def _fake_layer(seed=0):
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    # fp8-representable values: small integers scaled by a per-block power of two
+    q = torch.randint(-6, 7, (N, K), generator=g).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.randint(120, 130, (N, K // 32), generator=g).to(torch.uint8)  # 2^-7 .. 2^2
+    return q, scale
+
+
+def test_dequantize_applies_per_block_power_of_two():
+    q = torch.ones(2, 64, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.tensor([[127, 128], [126, 130]], dtype=torch.uint8)  # 2^0, 2^1 / 2^-1, 2^3
+    w = mxfp8_dequantize(q, scale)
+    assert torch.equal(w[0, :32], torch.ones(32)) and torch.equal(w[0, 32:], torch.full((32,), 2.0))
+    assert torch.equal(w[1, :32], torch.full((32,), 0.5)) and torch.equal(w[1, 32:], torch.full((32,), 8.0))
+
+
+def test_dequantize_rejects_wrong_scale_shape():

+class _TELinear(torch.nn.Module):
+    """A TE linear as it looks after the first FP8 forward: it holds a weight workspace."""
+
+    def __init__(self, quantized: bool):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(4, 64), requires_grad=False)
+        if quantized:
+            self._fp8_workspaces = {"weight": object()}
+
+
+class TransformerLayer(torch.nn.Module):  # name matters: the audit looks for *TransformerLayer*
+    def __init__(self, layer_number: int, quantized: bool):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.layer_number = layer_number  # mcore: 1-based, global across PP
+        self.self_attention = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.self_attention.linear_qkv = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.self_attention.linear_proj = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.mlp = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.mlp.linear_fc1 = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.mlp.linear_fc2 = _TELinear(quantized)
+
+
+class _Chunk(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, quantized_layers, n=N_LAYERS):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.embedding = torch.nn.Embedding(10, 4)
+        self.decoder = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.decoder.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList([TransformerLayer(i + 1, i in quantized_layers) for i in range(n)])
+        self.output_layer = torch.nn.Linear(4, 10)  # mcore ColumnParallelLinear: never TE
+

+def _hf_names(n=N_LAYERS, router=None, experts=None):
+    """Qwen/Llama-style dense names; ``router`` adds a router weight per layer, ``experts`` a
+    (prefix, [leaf names]) pair adding two experts per layer, e.g. ("block_sparse_moe.experts", ["w1", "w2", "w3"])."""
+    names = ["model.embed_tokens.weight", "model.norm.weight", "lm_head.weight"]
+    for i in range(n):
+        p = f"model.layers.{i}."
+        names += [
+            p + "self_attn.q_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.k_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.v_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.o_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.q_norm.weight",
+            p + "mlp.gate_proj.weight",
+            p + "mlp.up_proj.weight",
+            p + "mlp.down_proj.weight",
+            p + "input_layernorm.weight",
+            p + "post_attention_layernorm.weight",
+        ]
+        if router:
+            names.append(p + router)
+        if experts:
+            prefix, leaves = experts
+            for e in range(2):
+                names += [f"{p}{prefix}.{e}.{leaf}.weight" for leaf in leaves]
+    return names
+
+
+def _preset_quantizes(name):
+    """What the MXFP8 preset with no extra ``ignore`` sends quantized: the projections and the experts."""
+    return name.endswith("_proj.weight") or ".experts." in name
+
+
+def _export(names, quantizes=_preset_quantizes):
+    """The weight stream after the rollout quantizer: an FP8 weight plus its scale, or the BF16 weight."""
+    stream = []
+    for name in names:
+        if quantizes(name):
+            stream.append((name, torch.zeros(4, 64, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)))
+            stream.append((name + "_scale", torch.zeros(4, 2, dtype=torch.uint8)))
+        else:
+            stream.append((name, torch.zeros(4, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)))
+    return stream
+
+
+def _recorded(names, quantizes=_preset_quantizes):
+    auditor = TrainExportAudit("warn")
+    list(auditor.wrap_export(iter(_export(names, quantizes))))
+    return auditor.exported
+
+
+def _problem_names(problems):
+    return {p.split(":")[0] for p in problems}

+    # sync 1: workspaces present (layers 0 and 3 kept bf16 in training) -> runs, warns, marks done
+    list(auditor.wrap_export(iter(weights)))
+    problems = auditor.compare_with_training([_Chunk(quantized_layers={1, 2})])
+    assert len(problems) == 2 * 7 and auditor.finished  # 7 projection weights per bf16 layer
+    assert "training and the exported weights disagree on 14 weight(s)" in caplog.text
+    # later syncs: pass-through, no re-run
+    assert list(auditor.wrap_export(iter(weights))) == weights and auditor.compare_with_training([]) is None

+def test_create_arms_only_for_a_te_fp8_trainer_with_a_quantized_rollout(monkeypatch, caplog):

+def test_record_runs_the_comparison_when_the_weight_stream_ends():
+    # Wrapping the producer's stream is enough: the verdict does not depend on which sync route consumes it.
+    aud = TrainExportAudit("warn", engine="sglang")
+    weights = _export(_hf_names())

+"""CPU tests for the quantized-rollout sentinel."""
+
+import json
+import logging
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+

+
+from verl.utils.quant_sentinel import (
+    QuantizedRolloutSentinel,
+    check_quantized_rollout_metrics,

+)
+
+HEALTHY = {
+    "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": 0.014,
+    "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1,
+    "rollout_corr/kl": 0.007,
+    "response_length/clip_ratio": 0.03,
+}
+
+
+def _cfg(quantization, model_path=None, ignore_eos=False, response_length=None):
+    rollout = {"quantization": quantization, "ignore_eos": ignore_eos, "response_length": response_length}
+    return SimpleNamespace(actor_rollout_ref=SimpleNamespace(rollout=rollout, model=SimpleNamespace(path=model_path)))
+
+
+def _structured(**fields):
+    # rollout.quantization as the trainer config holds it: always present, all fields null when off.
+    return {"linear": None, "moe": None, "ignore": [], "config_file": None, **fields}
+
+
+def test_healthy_metrics_pass():
+    s = QuantizedRolloutSentinel("mxfp8")
+    for step in range(5):
+        s.check(HEALTHY, step)
+
+
+def test_nan_rollout_probs_raise():
+    s = QuantizedRolloutSentinel("mxfp8", mode="raise")
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="non-finite"):
+        s.check({**HEALTHY, "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": float("nan")}, 1)
+
+
+def test_nan_probs_with_empty_batch_is_not_flagged():
+    # valid == 0 means the batch had no tokens to compare, not that the rollout is broken
+    s = QuantizedRolloutSentinel("mxfp8")
+    s.check({**HEALTHY, "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": float("nan"), "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 0}, 1)
+
+
+def test_runaway_kl_raises():
+    s = QuantizedRolloutSentinel("mxfp8", mode="raise")
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="rollout_corr/kl"):
+        s.check({**HEALTHY, "rollout_corr/kl": 7.2}, 1)  # the FlashInfer stale-scale signature
+
+
+def test_all_truncated_needs_consecutive_steps():
+    at_cap = {**HEALTHY, "response_length/clip_ratio": 1.0, "response_length/max": 256}
+    s = QuantizedRolloutSentinel("mxfp8", mode="raise", clip_steps=2, response_cap=256)
+    s.check(at_cap, 1)  # one step: could be a hard batch
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="length cap"):
+        s.check(at_cap, 2)
+    s2 = QuantizedRolloutSentinel("mxfp8", mode="raise", clip_steps=2, response_cap=256)
+    s2.check(at_cap, 1)
+    s2.check({**at_cap, "response_length/clip_ratio": 0.4}, 2)  # streak resets
+    s2.check(at_cap, 3)

+def test_unquantized_rollout_is_never_checked():
+    s = QuantizedRolloutSentinel(None)
+    s.check({**HEALTHY, "rollout_corr/kl": 50.0, "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": float("nan")}, 1)

+def test_env_disable(monkeypatch):

+    s = QuantizedRolloutSentinel.from_config(_cfg("mxfp8"))
+    s.check({**HEALTHY, "rollout_corr/kl": 50.0}, 1)
+
+
+def test_trainer_hook_caches_sentinel_and_reads_config(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL", "raise")
+    trainer = SimpleNamespace(config=_cfg("mxfp8"))

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(

+"""CPU tests for the export-vs-engine format check and its vLLM name resolution (vLLM modules faked)."""
+
+import importlib.util
+import logging
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.quant_sync_format_check import SyncFormatCheck
+
+_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+
+
+def _load_by_path(name, relpath):
+    # verl.utils.vllm's package __init__ imports vLLM itself; this module needs only torch.
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, _REPO_ROOT / relpath)
+    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+_vllm = _load_by_path("vllm_sync_format_check_under_test", "verl/utils/vllm/vllm_sync_format_check.py")
+resolve_vllm_param, vllm_sync_format_check = _vllm.resolve_vllm_param, _vllm.vllm_sync_format_check
+
+FP8, BF16, U8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.bfloat16, torch.uint8
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _audit_logs_reach_caplog(caplog, monkeypatch):
+    # The audit logger does not propagate (it writes to stderr on its own); attach caplog's handler to it.
+    monkeypatch.delenv("VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT", raising=False)
+    log = logging.getLogger("verl.utils.quant_layer_audit")
+    log.addHandler(caplog.handler)
+    level = log.level
+    log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
+    yield
+    log.setLevel(level)
+    log.removeHandler(caplog.handler)
+
+
+def _t(dtype, *shape):
+    return torch.zeros(*(shape or (4, 4)), dtype=dtype)
+
+
+def _param(dtype, *shape):
+    return torch.nn.Parameter(_t(dtype, *shape), requires_grad=False)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The check itself, on an engine whose parameters are looked up by name
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _engine(**params):
+    model = torch.nn.Module()
+    model.params = {name.replace("__", "."): _param(dtype) for name, dtype in params.items()}
+    return model
+
+
+def _check(model):
+    return SyncFormatCheck.of(model, "test", lambda m, name: m.params.get(name))
+
+
+def test_the_first_sync_is_checked_bucket_by_bucket_and_later_syncs_are_not(caplog):
+    model = _engine(a__weight=FP8, b__weight=BF16)
+    check = _check(model)
+    check.begin_sync()

+class _StandardTopKOutput(NamedTuple):  # sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk.StandardTopKOutput

+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor
+    router_logits: torch.Tensor

+class _TopKConfig:  # sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk.TopKConfig (the fields the probe reads)
+    top_k: int
+    use_grouped_topk: bool = False
+    renormalize: bool = True
+    num_fused_shared_experts: int = 0
+    custom_routing_function: Optional[Callable] = None
+    correction_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    routed_scaling_factor: Optional[float] = None
+    scoring_func: str = "softmax"

+class _BypassedTopKOutput(NamedTuple):  # sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk.BypassedTopKOutput
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor
+    router_logits: torch.Tensor
+    topk_config: _TopKConfig

+class _RoutingMethodType(enum.IntEnum):  # sglang.srt.layers.moe.utils.RoutingMethodType

+    DeepSeekV3 = 2
+    Llama4 = 3
+    RenormalizeNaive = 4

+class _TopK(torch.nn.Module):
+    """sglang ``TopK.forward_cuda``: the router logits themselves for FlashInfer TRT-LLM, a softmax top-k otherwise."""
+
+    def __init__(self, top_k=2, runner="standard", **cfg):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.topk_config = _TopKConfig(top_k=top_k, **cfg)
+        self.runner = runner
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, router_logits):
+        if self.runner == "trtllm":
+            return _BypassedTopKOutput(hidden_states, router_logits, self.topk_config)
+        top = torch.softmax(router_logits.float(), dim=-1).topk(self.topk_config.top_k, dim=-1)
+        weights = top.values / top.values.sum(-1, keepdim=True) if self.topk_config.renormalize else top.values
+        return _StandardTopKOutput(weights, top.indices.to(torch.int32), router_logits)

+class _QuantMethod:
+    use_mxfp8 = True
+    is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized = True
+
+    def __init__(self, resolved_backend=None):
+        self.calls = 0
+        # sglang >= 0.5.18 stores the resolved MXFP8 dense backend on the quant method
+        if resolved_backend is not None:
+            self.mxfp8_dense_backend = _Backend(resolved_backend)
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        self.calls += 1
+        layer.weight_scale_inv_swizzled = layer.weight_scale_inv.clone() + 1
+
+    def apply(self, layer, x, bias=None):
+        # A FlashInfer-style kernel reads only the derived copy; "+1" is the fake swizzle.
+        scale = layer.weight_scale_inv_swizzled - 1
+        return (x.float() @ mxfp8_dequantize(layer.weight.data, scale).t()).to(torch.bfloat16)

+class _Linear(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, resolved_backend=None):
+        super().__init__()
+        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            torch.randint(-6, 7, (4, 64), generator=g).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        self.weight_scale_inv = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.full((4, 2), 127, dtype=torch.uint8), requires_grad=False)
+        self.quant_method = _QuantMethod(resolved_backend)
+        self.weight_scale_inv_swizzled = self.weight_scale_inv.clone() + 1  # as after the initial load

+class _MoEQuantMethod:
+    """sglang ``Fp8MoEMethod`` with an fp8-serialized MXFP8 checkpoint on the CUTLASS MoE runner of sglang >= 0.5.16:
+    post-load processing swizzles the expert scales *in place* into a different shape."""
+
+    use_mxfp8 = True
+    is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized = True
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.calls = 0
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        self.calls += 1
+        # the copy the kernel reads is derived from the canonical scales present at this moment
+        layer._kernel_scales = (layer.w13_weight_scale_inv.data.clone(), layer.w2_weight_scale_inv.data.clone())
+        for name in ("w13_weight_scale_inv", "w2_weight_scale_inv"):
+            p = getattr(layer, name)
+            swizzled = p.data.reshape(p.data.shape[0], -1).clone() + 1
+            if p.data.shape == swizzled.shape:
+                p.data.copy_(swizzled)
+            else:
+                p.data = swizzled  # sglang's _copy_or_rebind on shape change

+class _MoE(torch.nn.Module):
+    """sglang ``FusedMoE`` stand-in. ``runner="trtllm"`` behaves like the FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner: w13 is stored as
+    ``[up; gate]`` and the layer only accepts the router logits (it routes inside the kernel: top-k, then softmax)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, experts=2, inter=64, hidden=64, random=False, runner="standard"):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.runner = runner
+        self.use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe = runner == "trtllm"
+        self.routing_method_type = _RoutingMethodType.Renormalize if runner == "trtllm" else None
+        self.moe_runner_config = types.SimpleNamespace(routed_scaling_factor=None)
+        self.formats_seen = []
+        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+        w13 = (
+            torch.randint(-6, 7, (experts, 2 * inter, hidden), generator=g)
+            if random
+            else torch.zeros(experts, 2 * inter, hidden)
+        )
+        w2 = (
+            torch.randint(-6, 7, (experts, hidden, inter), generator=g)
+            if random
+            else torch.zeros(experts, hidden, inter)
+        )
+        self.w13_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w13.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), requires_grad=False)
+        self.w2_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w2.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), requires_grad=False)
+        self.moe_ep_size = 1
+        self.moe_tp_size = 1
+        self.reduce_results = False
+        self.num_experts = experts
+        self.w13_weight_scale_inv = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            torch.full((experts, 2 * inter, hidden // 32), 127, dtype=torch.uint8), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        self.w2_weight_scale_inv = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            torch.full((experts, hidden, inter // 32), 127, dtype=torch.uint8), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        self.quant_method = _MoEQuantMethod()
+
+    def forward(self, x, topk_output):
+        """sglang FusedMoE.forward stand-in: routed sum of gated-MLP experts on the scales the kernel reads."""
+        from verl.utils.mxfp8_refit_check import mxfp8_moe_expert_reference
+
+        if self.runner == "trtllm":
+            assert isinstance(topk_output, _BypassedTopKOutput)  # flashinfer_trtllm.py: a bare assert in sglang
+            top = topk_output.router_logits.float().topk(topk_output.topk_config.top_k, dim=-1)
+            ids, weights = top.indices, torch.softmax(top.values, dim=-1)
+        else:
+            assert isinstance(topk_output, _StandardTopKOutput)
+            ids, weights = topk_output.topk_ids, topk_output.topk_weights
+        self.formats_seen.append(type(topk_output).__name__)
+        s13, s2 = self._kernel_scales
+        out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], self.w2_weight.shape[1])
+        for j in range(ids.shape[1]):
+            for e in ids[:, j].unique().tolist():
+                rows = ids[:, j] == e
+                y = mxfp8_moe_expert_reference(
+                    x[rows],
+                    self.w13_weight.data[e],
+                    s13[e],
+                    self.w2_weight.data[e],
+                    s2[e],
+                    up_first=self.runner == "trtllm",
+                )
+                out[rows] += weights[rows, j : j + 1].float() * y
+        return out.to(torch.bfloat16)
+

+            module_name, param = name.rsplit(".", 1)
+            getattr(getattr(self, module_name), param).data.copy_(t)

+scales when a layer is processed, and leave the parameter itself in a kernel layout. The
+stand-ins below do the same: processing stores the derived copy the kernel reads and
+flattens the parameter, and staging hands the loader a checkpoint-shaped parameter again,

+def _load_by_path(name, relpath):

+def _mxfp8(shape, seed):
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    # fp8-representable values: small integers scaled by a per-block power of two
+    q = torch.randint(-6, 7, shape, generator=g).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.randint(124, 130, (*shape[:-1], shape[-1] // 32), generator=g).to(torch.uint8)
+    return q, scale

+class CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8:
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):

+        layer.weight_scale = _param(layer.weight_scale.data.reshape(-1).clone())
+
+    def apply_weights(self, layer, x, bias=None):
+        return (x.float() @ mxfp8_dequantize(layer.weight.data, layer._kernel_scale).t()).to(torch.bfloat16)

+    pass

+class CompressedTensorsLinearMethod:
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        layer.scheme.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+    def apply(self, layer, x, bias=None):
+        return layer.scheme.apply_weights(layer, x, bias=bias)

+
+class CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod:
+    is_monolithic = False
+    topk_indices_dtype = None

+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        layer._kernel_scales = (layer.w13_weight_scale.data.clone(), layer.w2_weight_scale.data.clone())
+        for name in ("w13_weight_scale", "w2_weight_scale"):

+    layer.weight_scale = _param(scale)

+    def forward_modular(self, x, topk_weights, topk_ids):
+        s13, s2 = self._kernel_scales
+        out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], HID)
+        for r in range(x.shape[0]):
+            for j in range(topk_ids.shape[1]):
+                weight, e = float(topk_weights[r, j]), int(topk_ids[r, j])

+    staged = []

+        elif isinstance(getattr(module, "quant_method", None), CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod):

+            module.w2_weight_scale = _param(module.w2_weight_scale.data.reshape(E, HID, INTER // 32).clone())

+def _monolithic_experts(**routing):
+    """RoutedExperts on a monolithic kernel that, like vLLM's, routes inside and applies routed_scaling_factor."""
+    model = torch.nn.Module()
+    model.experts = layer = _RoutedExperts()
+    layer.quant_method.is_monolithic = True
+    layer.routed_scaling_factor = 1.0
+    for key, value in routing.items():
+        setattr(layer, key, value)
+
+    def forward_monolithic(x, router_logits):
+        s13, s2 = layer._kernel_scales
+        top = torch.softmax(router_logits.float(), dim=-1).topk(layer.top_k, dim=-1)
+        out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], HID)
+        for r in range(x.shape[0]):
+            for weight, e in zip(top.values[r].tolist(), top.indices[r].tolist(), strict=True):
+                if weight:
+                    w13, w2 = layer.w13_weight.data[e], layer.w2_weight.data[e]
+                    out[r] += weight * mxfp8_moe_expert_reference(x[r : r + 1], w13, s13[e], w2, s2[e])[0]
+        return (out * layer.routed_scaling_factor).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+    layer.forward_monolithic = forward_monolithic
+    return model
+

+at load time (swizzled / packed layouts). A weight sync rewrites the canonical
+``weight`` / ``weight_scale`` tensors; if the derived copy is not rebuilt, the
+kernel pairs fresh weights with stale scales and generates garbage while every
+sync-side check passes (observed on 2xB200 with SGLang 0.5.12 + FlashInfer
+CUTLASS: held-out accuracy 0.0 from step 0, kl 7.2, entropy ~ log(vocab), exit
+code 0). The failure is invisible to the sync path because the sync itself
+succeeded; only the kernel's *output* is wrong.
+
+What. After the engine-specific re-processing, run one MXFP8 linear layer's own
+``apply`` on a small random input and compare against a plain bf16 reference
+computed from the canonical fp8 weight and UE8M0 scale. The kernel quantizes the
+activation to MXFP8 internally, so a healthy layer differs from the reference by
+a few percent; a layer reading a stale or mis-laid-out scale differs by O(1).
+
+Knobs (environment variables, read at call time):
+
+- ``VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK`` — ``warn`` (default) logs a failed check and lets the
+  sync go on, ``raise`` stops the sync with ``RuntimeError``, ``0`` skips the checks.
+- ``VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL`` — relative-error threshold (default ``0.25``).
+- ``VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL`` — threshold for the MoE expert probe
+  (defaults to the linear threshold; the gated MLP compounds the activation
+  quantization noise of two GEMMs).
+
+MoE experts. The same stale-layout failure applies to the fused expert weights
+``w13`` / ``w2`` (their scales are rewritten in place by the MoE runner), so one
+local expert is probed the same way: every probe row is routed to that expert
+with weight 1.0 and the layer's own forward is compared against
+``silu(x @ w1^T) * (x @ w3^T) @ w2^T`` on the dequantized weights.

+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+import traceback
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+# verl configures the "verl" logger only in the driver; worker processes (trainer actors, vLLM/SGLang
+# workers) fall back to the root WARNING level and would drop the INFO evidence lines below.
+logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))
+
+MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE = 32
+_DEFAULT_TOL = 0.25
+_PROBE_ROWS = 8
+# First successful probe per (engine, kind) is logged at INFO so a run leaves the measured kernel error
+# in its log without a negative test; later probes go to DEBUG.
+_ANNOUNCED: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
+
+
+def _announce(key: tuple[str, str], msg: str, *args) -> None:
+    if key in _ANNOUNCED:
+        logger.debug(msg, *args)
+    else:
+        _ANNOUNCED.add(key)
+        logger.info(msg, *args)
+
+
+class _NonFiniteReference(ValueError):
+    """The dequantized reference holds NaN/Inf: the canonical weight or scale the check reads is not valid."""
+
+
+_NON_FINITE_REFERENCE = (
+    "the dequantized reference is not finite: the canonical weight or scale the check reads holds NaN/Inf codes "
+    "(UE8M0 0xFF is NaN), typically a scale the weight sync never wrote and left at its staging fill, or NaNs in "
+    "the trainer's weights"
+)
+
+
+def _describe_probe_error(err: BaseException) -> str:
+    """``Type: message at dir/file.py:line`` of the innermost frame: a bare ``assert`` in an engine stays traceable."""
+    msg = str(err)
+    text = f"{type(err).__name__}: {msg}" if msg else type(err).__name__
+    frames = traceback.extract_tb(err.__traceback__)
+    if frames:
+        path = frames[-1].filename.replace(os.sep, "/").split("/")
+        text += f" at {'/'.join(path[-3:])}:{frames[-1].lineno}"
+    return text
+
+
+def refit_check_mode() -> str:
+    """``VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK``: ``warn`` (default), ``raise`` or ``0`` (off)."""
+    return os.environ.get("VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK", "warn").strip().lower()
+
+
+def refit_check_enabled() -> bool:
+    return refit_check_mode() not in ("0", "off", "false")
+
+
+def report_refit_check_failure(msg: str) -> None:
+    """Raise ``msg`` under ``VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=raise``; otherwise log it and let the sync go on."""
+    if refit_check_mode() == "raise":
+        raise RuntimeError(msg + " VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=warn only logs this, =0 skips the check.")
+    logger.warning("%s The sync goes on; VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=raise stops it here, =0 skips the check.", msg)
+
+
+def refit_check_tolerance() -> float:
+    return float(os.environ.get("VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL", str(_DEFAULT_TOL)))
+
+
+def refit_check_moe_tolerance() -> float:
+    return float(os.environ.get("VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL", str(refit_check_tolerance())))
+
+
+def mxfp8_dequantize(qweight: torch.Tensor, scale_u8: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Dequantize a rowwise MXFP8 tensor to fp32.
+
+    ``qweight`` is ``[..., K]`` (fp8 e4m3fn, or any dtype castable to fp32) and
+    ``scale_u8`` is ``[..., K // 32]`` UE8M0: the multiplier is ``2 ** (u8 - 127)``.
+    """
+    k = qweight.shape[-1]
+    if k % MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"last dim {k} is not a multiple of {MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE}")
+    blocks = k // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE
+    expected = (*qweight.shape[:-1], blocks)
+    if tuple(scale_u8.shape) != expected:
+        raise ValueError(f"scale shape {tuple(scale_u8.shape)} does not match canonical {expected}")
+    q = qweight.to(torch.float32).reshape(*qweight.shape[:-1], blocks, MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE)
+    descale = torch.exp2(scale_u8.to(torch.float32) - 127.0).unsqueeze(-1)
+    return (q * descale).reshape(qweight.shape)
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def probe_mxfp8_linear(
+    apply_fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
+    qweight: torch.Tensor,
+    scale_u8: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    rows: int = _PROBE_ROWS,
+    seed: int = 0,
+) -> float:
+    """Relative error between the kernel's output and the dequantized reference.
+
+    ``apply_fn(x)`` must run the layer's own quantized GEMM on ``x`` of shape
+    ``[rows, K]`` (bf16) and return ``[rows, N]``.
+    """
+    n, k = qweight.shape[-2], qweight.shape[-1]
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+    x = torch.randn(rows, k, generator=gen, dtype=torch.float32).to(device=qweight.device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    ref = x.to(torch.float32) @ mxfp8_dequantize(qweight, scale_u8).reshape(n, k).t()
+    if not torch.isfinite(ref).all():
+        raise _NonFiniteReference(_NON_FINITE_REFERENCE)
+    out = apply_fn(x)
+    if isinstance(out, tuple):  # some engines return (output, bias)
+        out = out[0]
+    out = out.to(torch.float32).reshape(ref.shape)
+    if not torch.isfinite(out).all():
+        return float("inf")
+    denom = ref.norm().item()
+    return float((out - ref).norm().item() / denom) if denom > 0 else float(out.norm().item())
+
+
+def assert_mxfp8_linear_matches(
+    name: str,
+    apply_fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
+    qweight: torch.Tensor,
+    scale_u8: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    engine: str,
+) -> float:
+    """Run the probe and report a failure with an actionable message (``report_refit_check_failure``).
+
+    Returns the measured relative error. Errors inside the probe itself (an
+    ``apply`` signature this engine version does not support, a CPU-only build)
+    are logged and skipped rather than reported: the check must never be the
+    reason a healthy refit fails.
+    """
+    tol = refit_check_tolerance()
+    try:
+        rel = probe_mxfp8_linear(apply_fn, qweight, scale_u8)
+    except _NonFiniteReference as err:
+        report_refit_check_failure(f"MXFP8 refit self-check failed on {engine} layer '{name}': {err}.")
+        return float("nan")
+    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - the probe is best-effort
+        logger.warning("mxfp8 refit check skipped on %s (%s): %s", name, engine, _describe_probe_error(err))
+        return float("nan")
+    if not rel <= tol:  # also fails a NaN error, which would compare as within tolerance
+        report_refit_check_failure(
+            f"MXFP8 refit self-check failed on {engine} layer '{name}': the layer's quantized GEMM disagrees "
+            f"with the dequantized reference by {rel:.3f} relative error (tolerance {tol}). This is the "
+            "signature of kernel scale layouts that were not re-derived after a weight sync (fresh weights "
+            "paired with stale swizzled/packed scales), or of a scale/weight layout the engine version "
+            "changed. Check the engine version against docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md, the selected MXFP8 GEMM "
+            "backend, and that this layer is meant to be quantized at all. VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL "
+            "loosens the threshold."
+        )
+        return rel
+    _announce(
+        (engine, "linear"), "mxfp8 refit self-check passed on %s (%s): rel err %.4f <= tol %.2f", name, engine, rel, tol
+    )
+    return rel
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# MoE experts
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def mxfp8_moe_expert_reference(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    w13_q: torch.Tensor,
+    w13_scale_u8: torch.Tensor,
+    w2_q: torch.Tensor,
+    w2_scale_u8: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    up_first: bool = False,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """fp32 reference of one gated expert on dequantized weights.
+
+    ``w13_q`` is ``[2I, H]`` in the fused-MoE convention (rows ``[:I]`` = w1 /
+    gate, rows ``[I:]`` = w3 / up; ``up_first`` for engines that store
+    ``[up; gate]``), ``w2_q`` is ``[H, I]``. ``x`` is ``[rows, H]``.
+    """
+    w13 = mxfp8_dequantize(w13_q, w13_scale_u8)
+    w2 = mxfp8_dequantize(w2_q, w2_scale_u8)
+    h = x.to(torch.float32) @ w13.t()
+    gate, up = h.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    if up_first:
+        gate, up = up, gate
+    return (F.silu(gate) * up) @ w2.t()
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def probe_mxfp8_moe_expert(
+    apply_fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
+    w13_q: torch.Tensor,
+    w13_scale_u8: torch.Tensor,
+    w2_q: torch.Tensor,
+    w2_scale_u8: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    reduce_ref: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor] | None = None,
+    up_first: bool = False,
+    rows: int = _PROBE_ROWS,
+    seed: int = 0,
+) -> float:
+    """Relative error between the MoE layer routed entirely to one expert and the dequantized reference.
+
+    ``apply_fn(x)`` must run the layer's own forward with every row of ``x``
+    (``[rows, H]`` bf16) routed to the probed expert with weight 1.0 and return
+    ``[rows, H]``. With tensor parallelism the caller passes the local expert
+    shards and ``reduce_ref`` (the same all-reduce the layer applies), so the
+    reference is summed the way the kernel output is. ``up_first``: the engine
+    stores ``w13`` as ``[up; gate]`` (see ``mxfp8_moe_expert_reference``).
+    """
+    hidden = w13_q.shape[-1]
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+    x = torch.randn(rows, hidden, generator=gen, dtype=torch.float32).to(device=w13_q.device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    ref = mxfp8_moe_expert_reference(x, w13_q, w13_scale_u8, w2_q, w2_scale_u8, up_first=up_first)
+    if reduce_ref is not None:
+        ref = reduce_ref(ref)
+    if not torch.isfinite(ref).all():
+        raise _NonFiniteReference(_NON_FINITE_REFERENCE)
+    out = apply_fn(x)
+    if isinstance(out, tuple):
+        out = out[0]
+    out = out.to(torch.float32).reshape(ref.shape)
+    if not torch.isfinite(out).all():
+        return float("inf")
+    denom = ref.norm().item()
+    return float((out - ref).norm().item() / denom) if denom > 0 else float(out.norm().item())
+
+
+def assert_mxfp8_moe_expert_matches(
+    name: str,
+    expert_id: int,
+    apply_fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
+    w13_q: torch.Tensor,
+    w13_scale_u8: torch.Tensor,
+    w2_q: torch.Tensor,
+    w2_scale_u8: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    engine: str,
+    reduce_ref: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor] | None = None,
+    up_first: bool = False,
+) -> float:
+    """MoE counterpart of ``assert_mxfp8_linear_matches``: report a mismatch, skip (warn) on probe errors."""
+    tol = refit_check_moe_tolerance()
+    try:
+        rel = probe_mxfp8_moe_expert(
+            apply_fn, w13_q, w13_scale_u8, w2_q, w2_scale_u8, reduce_ref=reduce_ref, up_first=up_first
+        )
+    except _NonFiniteReference as err:

+            f"MXFP8 refit self-check failed on {engine} MoE layer '{name}', expert {expert_id}: {err}."
+        )

+    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - the probe is best-effort
+        logger.warning(
+            "mxfp8 MoE refit check skipped on %s expert %d (%s): %s",
+            name,
+            expert_id,
+            engine,
+            _describe_probe_error(err),

+        report_refit_check_failure(
+            f"MXFP8 refit self-check failed on {engine} MoE layer '{name}', expert {expert_id}: the layer routed "
+            f"to this expert disagrees with the dequantized reference by {rel:.3f} relative error (tolerance "
+            f"{tol}). This is the signature of expert scales (w13_/w2_weight_scale) whose kernel layout was "
+            "not re-derived after a weight sync, or of a MoE runner whose scale layout the loader does not "
+            "know. Check the engine version and MoE backend against docs/low_precision/mxfp8.md. "
+            "VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL loosens the threshold."
+        )
+        return rel
+    _announce(
+        (engine, "moe"),
+        "mxfp8 MoE refit self-check passed on %s expert %d (%s): rel err %.4f <= tol %.2f",
+        name,
+        expert_id,
+        engine,
+        rel,
+        tol,
+    )
